text:
mia: Quick heads-up — spinning up iad-gpu2 cluster networking today. Need to validate transit peering, NAT for model pulls, DNS delegation, and egress perms. Planning window 13:00-15:00 PT. Who's available?
arjun: I'm on. What's the checklist?
sloane: tagging @ops-oncall. Did we request TGW attachment from net team or should I ping them?
net-bot: (Automated) VPC created: vpc-0a1b2c3d — private 10.12.0.0/16, public 10.13.0.0/24. Subnets: iad-a/iad-b/iad-c.
arjun: My steps: 1) attach TGW to iad-core 2) enable route table propagation 3) confirm RTs + no conflicts 4) deploy NAT GW in pub subnets 5) update egress firewall/security lists
arjun: Quick checks I'm running:
```bash
aws ec2 describe-transit-gateway-attachments --filters Name=vpc-id,Values=vpc-0a1b2c3d
aws ec2 describe-route-tables --filters Name=vpc-id,Values=vpc-0a1b2c3d
```
sloane: For model downloads we need NAT egress with TLS passthrough (no inspection). Plan: put NAT GW in az-a & az-b to reduce cross-AZ data. Cost note: NGW ~$0.045/hr + data out.
mia: DNS: we need to delegate private zone to Route53 and add records for bastion + kube API. @jules can you provision the zone and records? Also note split-horizon for corp names.
jules: I will. Plan: create private hosted zone gpu2.internal.redwood.com, associate with vpc-0a1b2c3d and add A for bastion, A for kube-api, CNAMEs as needed. Also will add resolver rules to forward corp queries to on-prem DNS.
ops-oncall: SNAT/ephemeral ports question — large model pulls spawn many connections. AWS NAT scales but watch ephemeral exhaustion. Recommend 2 NGWs per AZ & monitor ports.
arjun: Validation commands for later:
```bash
# from a private pod check outbound via NAT
kubectl exec -it test-pod -- curl -I https://models.s3.amazonaws.com
# verify TGW RT propagation
aws ec2 get-transit-gateway-route-table-associations --transit-gateway-route-table-id tgw-rtb-0123
```
mia: After you validate, I'll hand off to eng-sre for runbook + monitoring. Need these: route tables propagated, NAT active, DNS delegated, egress smoke tests pass, cost estimate for expected egress.
arjun: Note: found CIDR overlap with iad-core peering — they already advertise 10.12.0.0/16 elsewhere. I've changed the cluster CIDR to 10.14.0.0/16 to avoid conflicts, pushing terraform now.
sloane: Nice catch. Confirm when TGW propagation picks up new CIDR.
net-bot: TGW attachment tgw-attach-0f9a12 complete. State: available.
jules: DNS delegation created: hosted zone gpu2.internal.redwood.com (Z3GPU2) associated to vpc-0a1b2c3d. Records added: bastion -> 10.13.0.10, kube-api -> 10.13.0.20. Forwarder rule to corp DNS set.
ops-oncall: Egress smoke: from 5 test pods parallel downloading 2GB artifact from S3 — success, no 502s. NAT metrics: healthy 98%, no port exhaustion spikes.
arjun: PR for terraform (CIDR + NATs) submitted: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/pull/824 — includes 2 NGWs per AZ and route propagation config.
mia: I'll create monitoring widgets: TGW attachment state, route table diffs, NAT CloudWatch errors, Route53 resolver latency. Will open ticket for runbook authoring and assign to eng-sre.
sloane: Cost callout: if model pulls >10TB/mo we hit ~$3k extra egress + NAT charges. Add budget guardrail and an alert.
arjun: Running final validation commands now, posting results in thread.
net-bot: (Automated) post-deploy checks: TGW routes propagated: yes; NAT active: yes; R53 zone associated: yes; egress smoke: passed.
jules: handing to @eng-sre for runbook and long-term monitoring.
ops-oncall: Oncall ack. I'll watch metrics for next 48h and respond to alerts.
mia: All good — if no objections I'll mark this network bring-up complete and start runbook doc. :thumbsup:
net-bot: (Automated) Checklist complete: 6/6
